availability.p: In order to protect and preserve this artefact, access to it is restricted, and readers are asked to work from reproductions and published descriptions as far as possible. If you require access to the original, please submit your request through the Bodleian Archives and Manuscript Request service. When your request is received, you will be asked to provide further information outlining the subject of your research, the importance of this item to that research, and the resources you have already consulted. Your application will then be considered by our curatorial staff. Entry to read in the Library is permitted only on presentation of a valid reader's card (for admissions procedures contact Bodleian Admissions).

msContents.summary: Fragment 1; f. 1r–1v. Fragment of a Pataragamatoyc‘ (Liturgicon). The recto preserves the end of a rubric specifying the days on which the Divine Liturgies of St Basil of Caesarea and St John Chrysostom are to be celebrated. The verso bears a gold-ground miniature of an officiating bishop, possibly St Basil, before a canopied altar.

msItem.title: Pataragamatoyc‘ (Liturgicon), fragment
msItem.note: Folio 1r: Conclusion of rubric governing the choice of Basil’s or Chrysostom’s liturgy.
msItem.explicit: …Բայց զաւետիս Աստուածածնին յոր ինչ աւր գայ յայն տաւնեա ի փառս Քրիստոսի…
msItem.note: Folio 1v: Gold-ground miniature of an officiating bishop, possibly St Basil, before a canopied altar.

Parallel recorded in the examination worksheet: Munich, BSB Cod.armen. 6, ff. 205v–206r, images 424–425, The rubric follows Chrysostom’s liturgy; Basil’s portrait is on f. 206v and his liturgy begins on f. 207r.

msItem.note: Folios 4r–7v: Maštoc‘, Service for the Burial of a Priest. Fragmentary portions of the service. On f. 5v, a rubric directs the priests to make the sign of the cross over the body, place it on the bier, and lift and carry it.

msContents.summary: Fragment 6/7/8; ff. 10r-12v; Fragments of a Lectionary (Čašocʿ): Contains portions of the week of St Hripʿsimē and her companions, including the commemorations of Gayanē and her companions, John the Baptist and Athenogenes, and St Gregory’s emergence from the pit (f. 10). Readings from Romans and Mark precede the feast of Šołakatʿ (f. 11). The final folio preserves portions of the sixth and seventh days of the octave of the Exaltation of the Cross (f. 12).

decoDesc.decoNote: A horizontal band of stylised fruit and foliage, painted in green and blue on a gold ground, runs across the bottom of the page. Blue ropework bands on gold rise from it on either side and meet a matching band of fruit and foliage at the top, which stops short of the page edges. Inside this rectangular frame is a purple diaper pattern, edged towards the text by a red oval band with pointed projections. Above the frame are three peacocks in blue, red and gold. The two outer birds are shown in profile, with their beaks turned towards the central peacock, which faces the reader with its tail spread. A blue ropework arabesque on gold fills each upper corner. Blue branches in the side margins bear round green fruit veined with gold. On the left, a red snake rears up to taste the fruit.

msContents.summary: Fragment 13; f. 17r–v. Aṙakʿel Bałišecʿi, Tał Yovasapʿu (Տաղ Յովասափու), vv. 133–168. Barlaam comes to Josaphat in the guise of a merchant offering a precious pearl. The fragment preserves his exchange with the prince’s servant and the opening of his conversation with Josaphat.

msItem.author: Aṙakʿel Bałišecʿi
msItem.title: Tał Yovasapʿu, verses 133–168 (fragment)
Տաղ Յովասափու
msItem.note: Folio 17v · Verses 133–150. Barlaam arrives in the city disguised as a merchant and goes to the door of the king’s son. He tells Josaphat’s servant about his precious pearl and begins to describe its powers. The first surviving line ends «… ճգնաւորն ընտրեալ».

Folio 17r · Verses 151–168. The account of the pearl’s powers continues. The servant reports Barlaam’s words to Josaphat and brings him in. Josaphat asks to see the pearl, and Barlaam asks him to listen first.
Edition reference recorded in the examination worksheet: Ghazinian (Yerevan 1971), pp. 247–249.

msContents.summary: Fragment 14; Folio. 18r-18v; Modern paper sheet with sketches of four Armenian inscriptions from Seleucia and Korykos in Cilicia.

msItem.title: Sketches of four Armenian inscriptions from Seleucia and Korykos in Cilicia
msItem.textLang: Armenian inscription sketches with English annotations.
msItem.note: Folio 18r: Inscription sketches: A: Inscription in relief above the entrance gate of the castle at Seleucia. B: Incised inscription inside the same castle. C and D: Two inscriptions in relief on a castle tower at Korykos, labelled “Korghos” on the sheet.
Folio 18v։ Reference that appears to read “pp. 300 + 339, Vol. 2”. Also bears a pencil gift note and a Bodleian stamp dated 27 October 1919.

The handwritten reference to pp. 212, 217 and 236 corresponds to Francis Beaufort’s Karamania (1817), which illustrates the Seleucia gate inscription and describes the inscriptions at both sites. This item is probably associated with the correspondence between Francis Beaufort and Joseph von Hammer concerning inscriptions in Cilicia. Whether the sheet was enclosed with the surviving letter is uncertain.

history.acquisition: Given to the Bodleian on 27 October 1919, apparently with Unit 15. The donor’s name appears to read “Rev. E. Jermyn”, probably the Rev. Edmund Jermyn (1845–1925).

msContents.summary: Fragments 15; Folios 19r-23v; Letter from Joseph von Hammer, later known as Hammer-Purgstall, to Captain Francis Beaufort, FRS, in London. Written in Vienna in April 1818, apparently on 15 April. Hammer discusses Beaufort’s copies of Armenian, Arabic and Ottoman Turkish inscriptions in connection with the second edition of Karamania. The letter is accompanied by its addressed cover

msItem.author: Joseph von Hammer
msItem.title: Letter to Captain Francis Beaufort concerning inscriptions, April 1818, with its addressed cover
msItem.textLang: English, with Arabic and Ottoman Turkish passages, Roman-script transliteration and English translation.
msItem.note: Ff. 19r–22v: Letter on inscriptions. Hammer reports consulting the Armenian fathers and comments on the difficulty of deciphering the copies. He proposes readings for inscriptions at Anamour and Alaya, gives an Arabic reading of a Seljuk royal genealogy, and transcribes and translates an Ottoman Turkish verse that he compares with one from a bath in Bursa. The signature is visible on f. 22r.
Folio 23r: Front of cover of envelope. Addressed to Captain Beaufort, Fellow of the Royal Society, London. Also bears the endorsement and pencil gift note.
Folio 23v : Back of cover of envelope

supportDesc.condition: Fold creases, scattered staining and ink show-through. The cover is more heavily stained than the letter leaves.

handDesc.handNote: Letter in English cursive, with passages in Arabic script, Roman-script transliteration and English translation.

decoDesc.decoNote: Bodleian stamp on f. 19r. The cover bears an endorsement referring to two letters from Von Hammer about inscriptions at Seleucia and elsewhere, and a faint pencil note.

history.origin: Written in Vienna in April 1818, apparently on 15 April; addressed to Captain Francis Beaufort in London.
history.acquisition: A pencil note on the cover (f. 23r) records its donation to the Bodleian Library on 27 October 1919 by “Rev. E. Jermyn”, probably the Rev. Edmund Jermyn. A matching gift note on f. 18v suggests that the letter and the inscription sketches in Unit 14 entered the library together.
